identity.title: First analysis of solar structures in 1.21 mm full-disc ALMA image of the Sun

paper_type_evidence.quote: A full disc solar image at 1.21 mm obtained on December 18, 2015 during a CSV-EOC campaign with ALMA is calibrated and compared with full disc solar images from the same day

question.value: Can different solar structures (quiet Sun, active regions, prominences, inversion lines, coronal holes, coronal bright points) be identified in a 1.21 mm full-disc ALMA image, and what are their brightness temperatures relative to the quiet Sun?

evidence.quote: The second aim is to measure the intensities (brightness temperatures) of those structures and to compare them with the corresponding quiet Sun level.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00020.SV.
The measurement frequency/wavelength belongs to Band 6, which is one of the ten ALMA observing bands.

arrays.value: single 12 m total power antenna (PM03), double circle scan

evidence.quote: by scanning the solar disc with a 12 m single dish total power ALMA antenna (PM03) at a frequency of 248 GHz
The beam size amounts to 26 arcsec.
lasted for about 13 minutes
The measurement started at 20:12:21 UT on December 18, 2015

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: CSV campaign data released as science verification data

evidence.quote: A first part of the CSV data was recently released to the scientific community

provided.value: EUV/UV filtergrams and magnetogram for comparison

evidence.quote: various SDO images (a composite AIA image at 30.4 nm, 21.1 nm, and 17.1 nm; AIA filtergrams at 170 nm, at 30.4 nm, and at 19.3 nm; and a HMI magnetogram)
in H$\alpha$ line (Cerro Tololo Observatory, NISP)
in He I 1083 nm line core (NSO SOLIS)

pipeline_or_manual.value: two-load method with antenna efficiency factor C = 1.16

evidence.quote: A two-load method was used to calibrate the data
a correction (multiplication) factor $C$ was applied to account for the antenna efficiency: $C = 1.16$ for Band 6
The final uncertainty in the brightness temperature is about 5 % (cite: White2017).

evidence.loc: 3 An analysis of the ALMA image and comparison with other data
evidence.quote: The size of a pixel is about 3 arc sec.

what.value: Calibration, imaging and total-power procedure, correction factor C and 5% uncertainty

evidence.quote: More information about the measurements, calibration and imaging of the solar observations with ALMA for the single dish/total power mode can be found in the paper by (cite: White2017).

unstated_but_needed: Calibrated ALMA map file/version and exact CASA version
Coordinates and pixel positions of the regions of interest
Alignment procedure of ALMA map with SDO/Halpha images
Selection of the 56 coronal bright points
How the prominence region was extracted from Halpha

method.value: Two-load calibration with efficiency factor, data reduction in CASA

evidence.quote: Data reduction was performed using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) package
$C = 1.16$ for Band 6

analysis_steps.goal: measure brightness temperatures of regions of interest

method.value: Mean of all pixels in regions of interest; compared with quiet Sun at same radius along the equator east; AR threshold Tb>6900 K, sunspot Tb<6400 K

evidence.loc: 3 An analysis of the ALMA image and comparison with other data
evidence.quote: Brightness temperatures of various structures are calculated as the mean values of all pixels within regions of interest denoted in Fig. 1a.

key_parameters.value: QS circle radius 5 pixels at disc centre, 30 pixels elsewhere

evidence.loc: 3 An analysis of the ALMA image and comparison with other data
evidence.quote: At the solar disc center radius of the circle is 5 pixels, while for all other quiet Sun measurements it is 30 pixels.

validation.value: Selection criteria acknowledged as crude and arbitrary

evidence.loc: 3 An analysis of the ALMA image and comparison with other data
evidence.quote: We note that this selection criteria (for AR1 and SS) are crude and to some extent arbitrary.

analysis_steps.goal: identify coronal bright points across wavelengths

method.value: 56 CBPs identified in AIA 19.3 nm marked with boxes and overlaid on He I 1083 nm and ALMA maps; visual comparison

evidence.quote: 56 coronal bright points (only point-like structures and small loops) are identified and denoted with blue boxes.

validation.value: Correspondence of CBPs used to test overlay/orientation precision at about 5 arcsec

evidence.quote: this spatial precision is in the order of 5 arc sec.
Data reduction was performed using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) package

results_numeric.quantity: Active region AR1 excess over QS

evidence.quote: The average brightness temperature of the measured part of the inversion line has a brightness temperature 170 K below the quiet Sun level.

results_numeric.quantity: CBPs corresponding to ALMA bright points

evidence.quote: the great majority (82 %) of all coronal bright points from the EUV image corresponds to the ALMA 1.21 mm bright points

results_numeric.quantity: CBPs corresponding to He I 1083 nm dark points

evidence.quote: the great majority (75 %) of all coronal bright points from the EUV image corresponds to He I 1083 nm dark points
The amount of this limb brightening is in the order of 10 % in agreement with recent results of (cite: Alissandrakis2017).

findings_qualitative.value: Active regions are bright, sunspots dark, prominences and coronal holes barely discernible; inversion lines dark; coronal bright points appear as ALMA bright points.

evidence.quote: Magnetic inversion lines appear as large, elongated dark structures and coronal bright points correspond to ALMA bright points.

claims.hypothesis: Coronal bright points are detectable in the 1.21 mm ALMA image
claims.experiment: Overlay of 56 EUV-identified CBPs on He I and ALMA maps
claims.result: 82% match ALMA bright points, 75% match He I dark points
claims.finding: CBPs correspond almost one-to-one with ALMA bright points; overlay accurate to ~5 arcsec

evidence.quote: coronal bright points have almost a one to one correspondence with the ALMA 1.21 mm bright points

claims.hypothesis: Structures show characteristic brightness temperature contrasts at 1.21 mm
claims.experiment: Mean Tb in regions of interest versus QS at same radius

evidence.quote: These observational results are in general agreement with sparse earlier measurements at similar wavelengths.

why_this_data.value: Day chosen for availability of other-wavelength images, especially He I 1083 nm

evidence.quote: The observing day December 18, 2015 was chosen because of availability of images in other wavelength ranges, especially He I 1083 nm

limitations_admitted.value: Selection criteria for AR and sunspot are crude and arbitrary; prominence result depends on ~5 arcsec overlay precision

evidence.quote: The reliability of this result depends on the overlying precision (in the order of 5 arc sec)

referee_caveats_inferred: Single image, single day, single structure per class
Visual CBP matching is subjective, no statistics or control sample
Differences of 50-100 K are comparable to the quoted scatter

data_public_as_stated.value: CSV data released to the community via ALMA science verification page

evidence.quote: A first part of the CSV data was recently released to the scientific community

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: <1 GB (single-dish map plus public context images)
reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and simple averaging, but ROI positions, alignment and CBP selection are not given.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Key results rely on visual identification and undisclosed region definitions.
